ShortDescription.Value: Emergency corridors, accidents that don't delete your traffic, and real towing.

Publish.LongDescription:
🚨 In vanilla, an ambulance queues at a red light like everybody else — and the traffic jammed behind a crash simply **evaporates**. This mod fixes the whole chain: getting there, the accident itself, and the clean-up afterwards.
## 🚑 Emergency corridor Cars ahead of a vehicle running with lights and siren pull to the side of their lane and a corridor opens up — a real *Rettungsgasse*. If that is not enough, the responder escalates step by step:
- ✅ Two-sided corridor along its whole route (configurable distance, default 120 m) - ✅ Traffic lights ahead switch green, so the queue can clear the crossing - ✅ Cars evade onto the shoulder when the responder is really stuck - ✅ Overtaking on a free parallel lane - ✅ Passing on the oncoming carriageway when there is a safe gap — and merging back in - ✅ Careful squeezing past cars that are boxed in themselves - ✅ **Pedestrians wait at the kerb** instead of strolling onto the crossing in front of the ambulance (vanilla only ever stops them at a red light) - ✅ Arrives and **stops at the scene** instead of circling the block forever
## 💥 Accidents that behave - ✅ **Traffic behind a crash waits instead of despawning.** This is the big one: on a fully blocked road vanilla finds no route past the wreck and quietly deletes the entire queue. - ✅ Cars approaching a wreck brake in time instead of piling into it - ✅ Settled wrecks are consolidated onto the outermost lane, so at least one lane stays passable — traffic squeezes past instead of dissolving
## 🚛 Real vehicle recovery - ✅ **Tow depot** — a new building that only recovers crashed vehicles, so its trucks go straight to the accident - ✅ **Tow truck** — a dedicated vehicle that actually **hauls the wreck away** instead of "repairing" it into thin air - ✅ The nearest capable van gets the job — or a tow truck from your depot if none is close - ✅ Recovery vehicles drive **directly** to the crash instead of finishing their road-repair round first - ✅ Amber beacons while responding, on scene and while towing - ✅ Traffic makes way for them too, and after 30 seconds stuck they force their light green and work through the jam
## ⚙️ Compatibility & safety - **No Harmony patches, no replaced game systems.** The mod writes vanilla component fields from its own small systems; towing adds two tiny marker tags that are safe to remove with the mod. - **Save games stay compatible** — adding or removing the mod at any time is tested. (After uninstalling, leftover tow-depot buildings simply lose their model and can be bulldozed.) - Works with right-hand and left-hand traffic cities. - Every feature has its own toggle in the settings, so you can run just the parts you want. - English and German localization.
## 🔧 Options Every step of the chain can be switched off individually: corridor distance, squeezing, clearing undecided lanes, parallel-lane overtaking, green lights, oncoming lane, recovery priority, accident despawn protection, wreck consolidation, tow depot, towing, dedicated tow truck.
## 💬 Feedback Found a case where a responder gets stuck, or traffic behaves oddly around an accident? Please report it — with a screenshot if you can. There is a verbose logging option that writes diagnostics to `Logs/ClearTheWay.log`; that log makes bug reports much easier to act on.
Form without login: https://forms.gle/C2Yg6GXH6cZwAcdW9
Form with login (to attach screenshots): https://forms.gle/Q6gyAGZtrC9qXg4AA

Publish.ChangeLog:
This release is about wrecks that actually get cleared, a corridor that stops changing its mind - and a simulation that runs measurably faster.
**Faster** - The mod costs noticeably less per simulation step. Measured on the same city at the same load: **+14% simulation speed** over the previous release, and the busier it gets the more it helps - with 50+ emergency vehicles running at once it was +19%. Over a 3.5-hour session the tick rate in the last twenty minutes was the same as in the first, so it holds up. - Almost all of it came from one place: the pass that holds pedestrians at the kerb. It was searching a cube of 40 m in every direction around every siren - including 40 m backwards, and 40 m up and down, which on a map with tunnels or elevated roads dragged whole extra layers of footpath into the search and then threw them away again. It now looks only along the stretch the responder is actually driving.
**A stability fix worth naming** - A recovery truck that was merely queueing in traffic used to be "rescued" every 15 seconds - teleported back onto the lane it was already standing on, forever. One 100-minute session logged 904 of these, none of which did anything. Worse, doing it rewrote lane bookkeeping behind the game's back, which can take the whole simulation down. That is gone.
**Wrecks get cleared** - Wrecks are hauled away and delivered instead of the truck giving up halfway. - A truck that is genuinely off the road network, or has not moved for about five minutes, is now removed and its wreck goes back into the queue for another one. Losing a single truck is much cheaper than an unstable save.
**The corridor commits** - The responder picks ONE shape - the classic single gap, a central channel on wide roads, or heading for a free lane - and sticks with it. Previously three separate tests ran every step and disagreed with each other, so a responder standing in one spot kept changing its mind about which way to go and therefore never went anywhere. - A responder squeezing between two cars side by side could stall completely: the game only ever ignores ONE obstacle, and with two stopped cars it flipped between them every step so neither was ignored. It noses its way out of that now.
**Cars pulled aside onto space that exists** - The room beside a lane is measured on the side the car is actually being pushed towards. On carriageways running against the road direction the mod measured the far side and handed out up to 4 m of clearance that was not there - which is what threw cars across parking bays and onto kerbs.
